name: Drupal
description: Drupal is an open-source, API-first content management system for building structured, composable digital experiences across websites and channels.
best_for: Higher education, government, healthcare, nonprofit, and enterprise organizations that need an open-source, highly customizable CMS with no vendor lock-in.
features: Layout Builder for visual page composition
Multisite support for managing multiple sites from one installation
Taxonomy system for content organization and classification
Enterprise-grade security with no vendor lock-in
Drupal CMS distribution with guided setup for marketers and site builders

alternatives.name: WordPress
alternatives.description: The world's most widely used CMS, powering everything from blogs to large-scale websites with a vast plugin and theme ecosystem.
alternatives.best_for: Individuals and businesses of all sizes needing a flexible, widely supported CMS

alternatives.name: Joomla
alternatives.description: An open-source CMS built entirely by volunteers, offering multilingual support and flexible permission structures.
alternatives.best_for: Organizations needing multilingual sites and granular user permissions

alternatives.name: Craft CMS
alternatives.description: A content-first CMS offering flexible content modeling and developer-friendly, headless architecture.
alternatives.best_for: Agencies and developers wanting flexible content modeling without rigid structures

pricing.starting_price: Free and open source; no Drupal licensing fees

tiers.name: Drupal core
tiers.notes: GPL-licensed open-source software with no licensing fees.

cons: Drupal has no software license fee, but production use still requires hosting, a supported PHP/web-server/database stack, updates, backups, security operations, and often implementation expertise.
The Drupal project itself does not sell a managed SaaS plan; organizations that want managed hosting, development, or commercial support must source those services separately.
